name: Plumping gloss (menthol / cinnamon)

lead: Plumping glosses give a short-lived, visibly fuller pout without filler. People use them for a quick boost before a photo or night out.

The active ingredients mildly irritate the lip skin, which causes temporary swelling and a tingling or warming feeling. Wikipedia names capsaicin, the compound in chili peppers, as one such ingredient, and menthol and cinnamon are other common ones. The swelling fades within a short time, and no clinical studies of these glosses were found.

paras: People apply the gloss like an ordinary lip product, alone or over lipstick, and reapply for the effect. Results appear within minutes and last a few hours at most.

Because the mechanism is irritation, redness, stinging or discomfort can be expected, and people with sensitive lips or allergies to the ingredients may react more strongly. No studies of adverse events specific to these products were found.

angle.text: Users apply tingling menthol or cinnamon glosses to get a short-lived, visibly fuller pout without filler. Mild irritation causes the lips to swell, and the effect fades. Little formal research covers these specific ingredients.

lead: Lip plumpers are cosmetics that make lips look fuller by irritating the lip skin and causing temporary swelling [1]. Wikipedia names capsaicin, the compound in chili peppers, as an ingredient; it does not discuss menthol or cinnamon-based products specifically [1].
No clinical studies of irritant plumping glosses were found, and no looksmaxxing-community sources were available for this entry.

paras: According to Wikipedia, lip plumpers work through irritation of the lip skin that produces swelling and a temporarily fuller look [1]. The same article places them within a broader history of lip augmentation that includes early paraffin attempts, liquid silicone in the 1960s and bovine collagen from about 1980 [1].
